messages:
sara: Heads-up — prod route /v1/chat is hitting capacity and we're seeing degraded p95. Thinking about switching on path-affinity fallback so sessions stick to a fallback lane instead of model swap. Thoughts?

tim: Do you mean affinity by session cookie or by X-Route-ID header? We currently read x-client-id then route.

sara: Prefer header-based so mobile clients can opt-in. Example: X-Route-Affinity: session-<id>. If header present then try lane with same affinity, else use usual nearest-lane selection.

leo: Concern: affinity could concentrate load. Need circuit-breaker to break affinity when lane saturates. We should add a short-circuit policy: if lane_util > 85% -> mark lane degraded and reroute by priority.

maria: Agreed. Also add a QoS token check so high-priority tenants keep affinity. E.g., header X-QoS: gold|silver|bronze -> gold never evicted unless critical.

ashley: Console UX: propose a toggle 'Enable path affinity fallback' + a rate slider and a breaker threshold. Also show which tenants are pinned to lanes.

tim: Implementation detail: route config proposal:
```
match: 
  path: /v1/chat
  methods: [POST]
affinity:
  header: X-Route-Affinity
  eviction_threshold: 0.85
  fallback_order: [local-cache, backup-small, backup-cpu]
```
We can add header override: X-Fallback-Force to force using a backup model for testing.

leo: For CB triggers, we need to emit three metrics: lane_util, lane_queue_ms, cb_open_count. Use these for alerting and dashboard.

maria: Also add telemetry: when fallback used, tag traces with fallback.reason and fallback.path_variant so evals can compare quality.

sara: One more: quota interactions — if tenant has low quota, fallback should prefer cheaper quantized model not the same-cost backup. So route should consider tenant.quota_tier.

ashley: UX mock: show a per-route "degradation drilldown" with timeline of fallbacks, lane health, and quick "rollback fallback" button. (Will share in figma)

ops-bot: Incident note: 2026-03-12 14:22 fallback spike on /v1/chat -> 4xx increase. Auto-suspend affinity for 10m.

tim: Can we have a soft header precedence? If client sends both X-Route-Affinity and X-Fallback-Force, Force wins. Document precedence.

leo: Agree. Also adding a short-lived affinity token TTL 30m to prevent sticky hotspots.

maria: I'll sketch the policy PR: will add new proto fields: affinity_header, affinity_ttl_secs, eviction_threshold, fallback_sequence, qos_override_header.

sara: Perfect. If nobody objects I'll open RFC and include sample dashboards + console wireframes. :thumbsup:

tim: +1

ashley: +1 — will sync with design.

maria: PR created: https://git.company/repo/pulls/1423

sara: Thanks everyone. Will follow up with rollout plan and canary steps.
